newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Arthur C. Clarke addresses "HAL 9000" by Internet.
newsitem.headline: Arthur C. Clarke addresses "HAL 9000" by Internet.

text.p: Space writer and visionary Arthur C. Clarke took part in Sri Lanka's first live 'cybercast' on Saturday, addressing an audience half way around the world via an Internet video link.

The 79-year-old space guru broadcast a birthday greeting to "HAL 9000", an 'intelligent' computer he envisioned in his 1968 book "2001: A Space Odyssey", which became operational on January 12 at the University of Illinois in the United States.

A digitised video image of Clarke, clad in a silver space jacket, was broadcast from Colombo's Cyber Cafe and projected on a large viewing screen at the University of Illinois and simultaneously broadcast over the Internet's World Wide Web.
The image and audio is to be rebroadcast on the Internet via a web site called www.HALbday.com, said R. Abdulhussein, director of the Cyber Cafe.
The British-born Clarke, author of scores of novels and non-fiction books, has been living in Sri Lanka for the past 30 years.
In the past half century, many of Clarke's predictions have come true, including his then-controversial 1945 outline of a network of geo-stationary communications satellites.
